answer: Fix the forecast bias before next season is locked: summer was over-forecast by [F7], costing [F8], and winter under-forecast by [F10], leaving stores out of stock.

That over-forecast of [F7] cost about [F8] to hold and mark down.

situation: A retailer that forecasts each seasonal range before buying stock.
complication: Forecasts missed in both directions, leaving excess stock in summer and empty shelves in winter.
key_question: How large were last season's forecast errors, and how should the forecast change before next season?

titles.situation: Last season's forecasts missed in both directions.
titles.options: Two ways to improve next season's forecast.
titles.recommendation: Review forecasts against recent sales before buying.
titles.roadmap: Change the process before the forecast is locked, then track error weekly.
titles.kpis: Two measures show the forecast is improving.
titles.risks: The main risk is overcorrecting and running short.

points: Forecast [F1] against sales of [F2] left [F6] units over.

hypotheses.text: The summer forecast was too high.

issue_tree.so_what: Over-forecasting ties up cash in stock that must be marked down.

chart.title: Summer forecast ran well above units sold.

issue_tree.finding: Winter was forecast below demand and stores ran out.
points: Forecast [F4] against sales of [F5], a shortfall of [F9].

hypotheses.text: Stockouts cost sales beyond the units sold.

issue_tree.so_what: Under-forecasting loses sales the stock-outs hide.

chart.title: Winter sales ran above the forecast.

issue_tree.finding: The errors run in opposite directions, so a single fixed adjustment would not work.
points: Summer error was [F7] and winter error [F10].

hypotheses.text: Forecasts are biased the same way every season.

issue_tree.so_what: The process needs a check against recent sales, not a fixed uplift or cut.

chart.title: Summer error was larger than winter error.

options.name: Recent-sales review
options.description: Check each range's forecast against recent weekly sales before the buy is locked.

options.name: Smaller first buys
options.description: Buy less up front and reorder in season as sales show.

recommendation.rationale: It catches errors like the summer's [F7] and the winter's [F10] before stock is bought, and costs little; the supply chain director decides.

actions: Agree the review step with the buying team before next season's forecast is locked.
Track weekly forecast error by range and store.

risks.mitigation: Review both over- and under-forecast ranges together.
Flag weeks with stock-outs before using sales as demand.
